title: Prove optimal 52-bit refined recovery over mode-preserving frames (no new κ)
body:
Resolve #5444's two-step mixed-refinement question for every fixed integer unimodular frame U preserving the actual eight mode projections. For H_U(x)=K(U K(2x)), the minimum worst-case recovery alphabet is 2,601,832,488,601,921 states (52 packed bits), versus 56 bits in the parity-I subclass. Optimality holds exactly when the binary images of M and U^-1 M are disjoint. Supplies an explicit sparse frame, full-output codec and a complementary finite-depth parity-I theorem.

Base: a7638a4ce2a29947457ae8d6bf8cd70a234dfeac.
#5444 source head: 9004eb1b185803ba2f3101b8955e6e8d0dc12ed4.
Exact fixture and predecessor Git/SHA256 pins: SOURCES.json.

Reproduce (Python 3.12, stdlib):
```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/refined-native-recovery
```
Expected: `PASS_REFINED_NATIVE_RECOVERY`, `PASS_INDEPENDENT_OPTIMAL_FRAME` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Executed: 400 optimal-codec and 384 chain roundtrips; independent 20,001 scalar cases, 65,536 binary pairs, 256 cosets, 224 inverse checks and 1,152 trajectories. Actual code/source mutations reject omitted parity, invalid frames and altered fixtures. Exact three-stage counterexample refutes one proposed proof extension, not the longer-chain optimum. Normal/-O, committed-byte/mode, export and read-only Git-free replays pass. Fixed domains; universal proofs are separate. Full-history preflight was not run in the shallow checkout.

No new κ. The output function changes. A linear consumer is compatible iff OV=0, but recovery still requires the full output. Restoring the old output without extra side information restores its 56-bit lower bound. Relative refinement, routing, codec workspace and cleanup remain payable; no selected caller or improved invoice is supplied. All five assumptions remain.

By @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in construction, independent proof/checking and caller-cost audit. Credit zxv (#5444), Ali Romman (#5323), Brian (#5035) and retained lineage. No human/proof-kernel acceptance.

Proof, pins, controls and limitations: https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/f184d2a0257c1cb56a820c5c123ec6d7ba878741/research/refined-native-recovery
Complete remote Git tree matches the tested contribution.
